Subject: Re: User-facing lag on live chat (starts ~20:50 UTC)

Jordan —

We started seeing intermittent pauses in our live chat widget around 20:50 UTC tonight. Messages sometimes arrive 6–12s after the user stops typing; streaming appears to stall mid-response. This is happening across a handful of sessions (see attached short logs). It affects our checkout support flow — engineers are seeing repeated sequence numbers for the same request.

Anything you can share on what changed on your side? We haven't modified our client. We're blocking traffic to fall back to polling, but that's not ideal.

Attaching a few tail logs and a sample transcript.

— Alex

Alex — thanks for the quick heads up and the logs. We're looking into this now.

Immediate notes and short-term mitigations you can apply while we triage (no code change required for most):
- Switch to non-streaming fallback: set stream=false for the chat route to avoid partial-frame stalls. This returns full responses and should reduce visible pauses.
- Lower max_tokens and response_window: reduce token budget to keep generation under 2s for your typical prompts.
- Disable batching for this API key: in the Console you can set routing->batching: off for the BrightCommerce key; that forces single-request hot-path and avoids batch-queue delays.
- Increase client-side socket timeout to 30s to avoid premature disconnects while we investigate.

We're opening an internal incident and will share progress. I'll loop in engineering and send a short RCA once we have root cause and timeline.

Jordan Blake

Thanks, Jordan. Quick triage notes from infra:
- At ~20:49 UTC there was a degraded node group in the west-us streaming pool that entered a slow-restart loop after a kernel patch rolled quietly on a small subset of hosts (we're still verifying cause). This caused increased tail latency for continuous-stream sessions that hit those hosts.
- Automatic routing attempted a retry path that inadvertently batched a subset of the stalled streams, which amplified delays for affected sessions.

Short-term mitigations applied (completed by 21:10 UTC):
- Evicted the bad node group from the streaming pool and drained affected shards.
- Temporarily disabled the aggressive batch-merge heuristic in the router for the west-us region.
- Pushed a conservative rolling restart to the pool (no client-visible configuration changes required).

Please relay these steps to the customer and advise the non-streaming fallback if they need immediate relief during their peak. We'll follow up with an engineering RCA and a permanent fix plan (patch + improved preflight checks).

I'm attaching a diagnostic capture from the streaming proxy (redwood_stream_diag.png).

— Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Jordan / Marissa — thanks for the fast response and the clear mitigation steps. We switched to stream=false and saw immediate improvement; rolling restarts look to have stabilized traffic for our sessions.

Two quick asks on our side:
1) Can you confirm whether this incident affected any persisted conversation state (we rely on server-side KV for some checkpoints)?
2) We'd like the postmortem and the timeline so we can review with our SREs.

Appreciate the attachment; we'll share that with our engineers. If you plan a scheduled maintenance window to apply the permanent fix, please give us a 48h heads up.

— Alex
